name: Iron Sword
description: A Merrowby smith's honest work: flat iron, a leather grip, a maker's mark of three struck lines. Every third house in the Vale keeps one behind the door and calls it the thatching knife, in case anyone asks.

name: Woodsman's Axe
description: Hedge-laying steel on an ash haft, meant for hawthorn and used on worse. Slower than a sword and it does not care: what it reaches, it opens. Woodfolk sharpen theirs on the standing stones and do not explain why.

name: Ash Greatsword
description: Carried south by the Tolling Order and left where its carrier stopped. The grey bloom on the blade is Cinderlea ash that will not polish out; pilgrims say a sword that has stood in the Choir keeps a little of the note, and swings heavier for it.

name: Hunting Knife
description: For skinning, cutting cord, and eating cheese in that order. Held low and out of the light it does the fourth thing it is for, which nobody in the Vale writes down.

name: Hunting Bow
description: Briarwold yew, backed with sinew and waxed against the wet. The Woodfolk have no law and no jail; they have this, and a custom about where they aim first.

name: Arrow
description: Goose-fletched, iron-piled, and marked at the nock with the owner's line so a quarrel over a deer stays a quarrel over a deer.

name: Round Shield
description: Lime boards, a rawhide rim, an iron boss dented twice. Warden recruits paint theirs with the name of their village, so that if the shield comes home alone the village is still said aloud.

name: Wool Tunic
description: Undyed Vale wool, mended at the elbow by someone who cared enough to match the thread. It turns rain, a thorn, and a very poor swing.
